title: Manage archive-backed skills and compose their global AGENTS index
description:
## Current reading

- [References](/refs/README.md): the brief domain introduction.
- [Skill process](/refs/skills.md): selection, composition, archive citations, and maintenance.
- [Core index](/refs/GLOBAL.md): concise skill links and the small OKF sources example for global context.
- [GLOBAL writing contract](/constitution/README.md#doc-constitution-global): the KISS default and scoped honing exception.

## Intent

Build a Rekon-owned tool for managing skills, composing our own skill offerings, and integrating their index into the making of our global AGENTS.md. Rekon should be our single entry point for selecting and advertising these capabilities. We already know where our archive lives: an upstream skill can remain in its repository checkout and be cited there.

This epic owns the general feature. Concrete upstream repositories are examples within it, not separate product-specific epics. The refs documentation and manual core index now exist. The manager command surface and automated composition/index generation remain design work.

## Why this matters

Useful skills arrive both alongside tools and in dedicated skill collections. Their existence should be usable without adopting each vendor’s installer, duplicating their content into harness-specific directories, or surrendering control of our ambient skill descriptions. We want to decide which capabilities agents see, when they should load them, and how upstream guidance joins our own practices.

## Initial design direction

- **Sources:** identify an upstream repository or our own maintained material, its local home, actual skill entry file, and support-file base. Prefer the existing `~/archive/<org>/<repo>` convention for upstream checkouts; keep canonical repository URLs as provenance.
- **Catalog:** maintain our chosen identities, useful activation descriptions, and source pointers. Upstream metadata can seed an entry; our catalog owns what is advertised. Discovery and selection are distinct operations.
- **Composition:** support our own authored skills and deliberate combinations of upstream guidance and local practice. Preserve who owns each body and make any local override or adaptation understandable.
- **Exposure:** generate a compact skill/tool index for global AGENTS.md with when-to-load cues and concrete archive citations. Load detailed material on demand, preserving the source directory for relative references and scripts.
- **Single entry point:** changes to our available skill set and its advertised routing flow through this tool/catalog. Define how this relates to native harness skill discovery so independently installed copies do not become competing catalog authorities.

The existing [`rekon agents` assembler](/constitution/agents-assembly.md) already handles explicitly selected GLOBAL fragments, provenance, deterministic output, and check mode. Design the skill-index contribution against that boundary. The live `/AGENTS.md` remains a manuscript today; production assembly cutover is tracked by `rekon-agents-maintenance` and is a separate decision from designing this capability.

## Examples

title: Model toward and away-from feature bearings
description: Give a Navigation explicit signed bearings over named features. A nav can say which product, architectural, operational, or experiential features the route goes toward and which it deliberately moves away from. Bearings may apply to the whole route, a leg, or an alternative branch, and must reference the named feature rather than duplicate an unstable prose description. Record why the bearing matters and what evidence would show movement. Keep feature bearings distinct from beads feature tickets: a bearing names a sought or rejected property; a work item may implement it but is not automatically the property itself. Absence of a toward bearing never implies away-from, and vice versa.
acceptance_criteria: The model expresses explicit toward and away-from relations to named features at route and leg or branch scope; each bearing can carry rationale, evidence or observable signal, and source or authority; omitted, unknown, neutral, conflicted, and explicitly opposed features remain distinguishable; alternatives can expose different bearings without collapsing them into one score; a feature may link to implementing work without being conflated with that ticket; examples include positive features, anti-features, a tradeoff, and a leg that advances one feature while retreating from another.

title: Model routes, beacons, forks, and rerouting
description: Turn the Navigation contract into a minimal route model that a human or agent can read and maintain. A route begins with a position fix, names an honest destination or heading, and connects them through legs, parallel tracks, beacons with observable arrival proofs, and decision forks. It must distinguish prerequisites from alternatives, place open decisions at the point where evidence can resolve them, mark deliberately off-route regions, and state switch and stop rules. Progress updates and reroutes must preserve prior course and explain what evidence, changed terrain, or authority caused the revision. The model orders by dependency and evidence, not by calendar.
acceptance_criteria: A Navigation can represent a position, destination or heading, sequential legs, parallel tracks, dependencies, beacons, arrival proofs, forks, decision stations, off-route branches, and switch/stop rules; the model distinguishes an unmet obstruction from an accepted imposition and an unknown region; route state and progress can be updated without erasing the prior route or source exploration; reroutes record cause, authority, and supersession relationship; examples show a complete route, a forked route, and a route that must stop; no field implies a time estimate or delivery schedule.

title: Define the Navigation knowledge contract
description: Define the semantic contract for a Navigation artifact before fixing a file template or tool API. State the distinction: Exploration expands and maps the space; Navigation chooses and explains a course from a known position toward an honest destination through that mapped space. Define the minimum concepts a nav must carry: sources and position fix, destination or heading, observable beacons and arrival proofs, ordered legs or tracks, dependencies, hazards and constraints, forks and decision stations, switch/stop/reroute rules, authority and prior decisions, status/provenance/staleness, and deliberately off-route regions. Clarify when a nav is inappropriate, how it differs from a schedule or issue graph, and how revisions preserve the exploration and prior route rather than rewriting history.
acceptance_criteria: The contract names Navigation and nav as the canonical type and shorthand; required versus optional concepts are explicit and justified; boundaries with Exploration, Design, Plan, Roadmap, and beads dependency graphs include concrete examples and counterexamples; route ordering is distinguished from calendar scheduling; authority, evidence, arrival, stop, reroute, supersession, and staleness semantics are defined; the Watchman assurance nav wave is analyzed as founding evidence without becoming the universal template; unresolved choices are recorded for the pilot rather than silently fixed.

title: Establish Navigation as a first-class knowledge type
description: Define and establish Navigation (short form: nav) as a durable Rekon knowledge type. An Exploration maps a possibility or problem space; a Navigation starts from an explicit position and charts a revisable route through that space. It names destinations and observable beacons, orders route legs by dependency or evidence, records forks and stop or reroute rules, and makes hazards visible. A nav may cite named features it is moving toward or away from without pretending those bearings are a scalar score, a delivery schedule, or an exhaustive plan. The recent Watchman assurance navigation wave is the founding case and evidence source, not a schema to copy blindly.
acceptance_criteria: Navigation has a documented type contract and explicit boundary from Exploration, Design, Plan, Roadmap, and issue dependency graphs; route topology and toward/away-from feature bearings are represented with named references and evidence; at least two real pilots demonstrate that the type is useful beyond one maritime metaphor; an authoring workflow exposes the accepted type without overwriting its source explorations; navigation remains revisable, authority-aware, and honest about unknown terrain.

title: Build a doc relay tool for passing documents between agents
description: Agents constantly need to hand documents to each other - subagent briefs, session handoffs, cross-repo references - and today that is ad hoc pasting into prompts with no provenance and no round trip. rekon already owns the adjacent pieces: combine merges prompt plans, interpolate renders them, project-files selects files. Add the missing relay: a pack side that selects docs by path/glob or topic directory (design/<topic>/, doc/<topic>/) and emits a bundle plus a manifest recording each doc's canonical source per the doc-linking conventions (bundle-root-relative paths, canonical URLs), origin (who/what produced it, when), and topic grouping; and an ingest side that lands a bundle into a target workspace namespaced so it never silently clobbers existing files. The manifest, not a blob dump, is the contract: it should be legible to an agent deciding what to read and in what order. Round-trip with combine/interpolate so a packed bundle can be consumed directly as an agent prompt. rekon-observe-deciduous-graph may inform how manifest entries reference each other (typed links vs flat lists) - coordinate rather than guessing. Write the design first in design/doc-relay/ per wave conventions before building.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc exists in design/doc-relay/ and is jj committed before implementation lands. Pack and ingest commands work end to end: a bundle packed from one workspace ingests into another with a manifest carrying canonical paths, origin, and topics. Ingest refuses to overwrite existing files without an explicit flag. At least one round trip through combine or interpolate is demonstrated. README documents the new command. Work is jj committed in logical groups.

title: Observe how deciduous models dependency mapping and node linking
description: Observation/research ticket, not an implementation commitment. notactuallytreyanastasio/deciduous (checkout at ~/archive/notactuallytreyanastasio/deciduous/, do not re-fetch) is decision-graph tooling for AI-assisted development: goal/decision/outcome nodes joined by typed edges in SQLite (diesel, schema/ + migrations/), surfaced to agents via CLI and MCP. Study specifically how it does dependency mapping and node linking: the node schema and type model; edge typing, directionality, and validation (are links checked at write time? cycle handling? lineage queries?); how links get created in practice (agent ergonomics of the CLI/MCP surface, stable IDs vs content addressing); and what the graph actually gets used for once it exists. Write findings to design/deciduous/ following wave conventions (deciduous0.<model>.md), then cross-reference into the doc-constitution and naming threads. This may later inform rekon-agent-doc-relay's reference model.
acceptance_criteria: Findings doc exists in design/deciduous/ citing real schema/ and src/ locations, not just README claims. Node model, edge model, and link creation/validation flow are each covered. Doc states explicitly what rekon should adopt and what it should avoid, with reasons. Doc includes canonical links to upstream files/URLs and is jj committed.

title: Add interpolation-execution mode to interpolate command
description:
After the interpolate command has been created, add an execution mode that can run the interpolated result as a shell command. This would allow users to interpolate variables into command templates and then execute them, similar to how opencode handles commands with interpolated arguments.

Example usage:
```bash
rekon interpolate -t 'echo "Hello $1"' world --execute
# Would output: Hello world

rekon interpolate -t 'ls -la $1' /tmp --execute
# Would run: ls -la /tmp
```

This would be useful for:
- Testing command templates with variable arguments
- Executing commands with variable substitutions without full opencode
- Creating reusable command templates with positional parameters
- Testing prompt/ file templates before using them with opencode
